objective: Validate whether the universal trace surface schema captures a real CLI session with enough fidelity for an operator agent to learn from it
findings_summary: CLI sessions have narrative structure — command sequences tell stories. Intelligence density is 3x higher than API per span. Cross-modality nesting (CLI wrapping API traces) confirmed.

response.body_summary: 12 modified files, 21 untracked files on schema-v0.2-batch1 branch

observation.what_happened: git status reveals 12 modified files and 21 untracked files on schema-v0.2-batch1 branch. Heavy uncommitted work spanning both packages.
observation.what_learned: CLI trace surface must capture STATE CONTEXT: which branch, what was modified, what was untracked. An operator agent seeing this trace knows there is significant uncommitted work spanning both packages.
observation.surprises: 21 untracked files means major new modules exist only locally.
questions_raised: Should cli_ext include a diff_summary field for modified files?

observation.what_happened: Three local branches, two remote. Current branch schema-v0.2-batch1 has no remote tracking — exists only locally.
observation.what_learned: Branch topology is a CLI-specific signal. An operator agent seeing this knows schema-v0.2-batch1 is unpushed — risk of work loss.
observation.surprises: The unpushed branch signal is proactive intelligence an operator could act on.

observation.what_happened: 395 tests pass in 1.36s across both packages (parser + trace-sdk). Zero failures.
observation.what_learned: Test execution has extremely high intelligence density. Running tests AFTER seeing uncommitted changes tells the operator the uncommitted work is validated. Cross-span correlation compounds intelligence.
observation.surprises: 395 tests — up from 177 two days ago. Growth rate is itself a velocity signal.
questions_raised: Should cli_ext capture test-level detail or just summary?

contains_contexts.description: Pipeline reads and classifies Plaid API trace files

response.body_summary: Pipeline converged in 2 iterations. 10 actions planned, 10 executed, 10 succeeded. Accuracy 1.0.

observation.what_happened: Pipeline converged in 2 iterations under the 3-iteration limit. 10 actions planned, 10 executed, 10 succeeded. Generated 5 FSM models, 1 error handler, 1 typed API client, 3 exploration directives.
observation.what_learned: This is the most intelligence-dense CLI interaction: a single command triggers a multi-stage pipeline and produces structured output AND generated artifacts. The CLI trace captures the entire BCI loop in one span.
observation.surprises: The pipeline itself is a CLI tool — CLI tracing captures IGNITE operating itself. Self-referential.
questions_raised: Should it carry dual modality tags (cli + internal)?

response.body_summary: 608 insertions, 23 deletions across 12 files. Net +585 lines.

observation.what_happened: 608 insertions, 23 deletions across 12 files in both packages. Net +585 lines.
observation.what_learned: The CLI session as a whole tells a story no individual command captures. The SEQUENCE of commands is the intelligence. An operator could recommend: commit and push — the risk is low.

findings.title: CLI sessions have narrative structure
findings.description: CLI sessions have NARRATIVE STRUCTURE that API traces lack. The sequence git-status→branch→test→pipeline→diff tells a coherent story. An operator agent needs session-level intent, not just individual command intent.

findings.title: CLI wraps other modalities — cross-modality nesting
findings.description: The ignite-parse CLI command internally processes API traces. CLI→API modality nesting is universal and needs contains_contexts to capture the relationship.
evidence: cli-004 processes Plaid API trace files through BCI pipeline

findings.title: CLI has highest intelligence density per span
findings.description: CLI traces are 3x denser than API per span. A single pytest span captures 395 test results. CLI commands aggregate many underlying operations.
evidence: pytest span: 395 tests in one observation
pipeline span: full BCI loop in one command
